# Slides & Presentation Design Guide

## Core Slide Rules

- **One idea per slide.** If a slide needs two headers, it's two slides.
- **Title is the takeaway.** Slide title = the conclusion, not the topic. "Revenue is growing" not "Revenue."
- **6×6 rule (maximum):** 6 bullets per slide, 6 words per bullet. Treat as upper bound, not target.
- **Never read slides aloud.** Slides support the speaker; they don't replace them.
- **Consistent template:** Same font sizes, same alignment, same color usage slide to slide.

## Slide Architecture by Deck Type

### Executive / Board Deck
- Slide count: 8–12 slides maximum
- Format: Title → Agenda (optional) → Situation / Context → Key data (1–2 slides) → Insight / So what → Recommendation → Ask / Next step → Appendix
- One chart or graphic per slide. Every chart needs a labeled takeaway title.
- No builds or animations — boards print decks or read async.

### Sales / Prospect Deck
- Slide count: 10–15 slides
- Format: Title → Problem (buyer's words) → Why now → Solution overview → Architecture/how it works → Proof (customer names/logos, ROI) → Differentiators → Pricing/packaging (optional) → Next step
- Open with pain — not product. Buyers decide in the first 2 slides whether to keep reading.
- Use customer logos only with permission. Use metrics wherever possible.

### Internal / Team Deck
- Slide count: As needed, but cut ruthlessly
- Format follows agenda structure
- Can be text-heavier than external decks
- Action items slide at end: owner, action, due date in a table

### Demo / Walkthrough Deck
- Minimal text — this is visual support for a live demo
- Screenshots over stock images
- Annotate screenshots with numbered callouts
- Include a "before/after" or "workflow" slide to anchor the story

## Layout Principles

**Visual hierarchy:**
- Title: Largest, most prominent (32–40pt)
- Body text: 18–24pt minimum — if it doesn't fit, cut the content
- Caption/footnote: 12–14pt

**Alignment:**
- All elements snap to a grid. Nothing floats arbitrarily.
- Left-aligned text blocks. Centered only for title slides and section dividers.

**Color:**
- Max 3 colors per slide (background, primary, accent)
- Use accent color to highlight 1 thing per slide — the most important element
- Dark text on light background for text-heavy slides; light text on dark for impact slides

**Images:**
- Full-bleed backgrounds: Use for title slides, section transitions
- Inline images: Align to a column, not centered mid-text
- No stock photo clichés (handshake, arrows pointing up, etc.)

**Charts and data:**
- Title = insight, not variable name (e.g., "ARR accelerating" not "ARR over time")
- Remove chart junk: grid lines, legends if labels are direct, 3D effects
- Highlight the relevant data point — gray out context data

## ChatGPT / AI Image Prompt Guidelines (for slide visuals)

When generating an image prompt for a slide visual:
- Specify: style, subject, color palette, aspect ratio (16:9 for slides), mood
- Format: `"[Style]: [Subject]. Color palette: [colors]. Mood: [tone]. 16:9 aspect ratio. No text."`
- Example: `"Clean enterprise tech illustration: secure server connected to multiple tools via glowing lines. Color palette: deep navy #0B1220, teal #00F0FF, indigo #4B5AE0. Professional, minimal, futuristic. 16:9 aspect ratio. No text."`
- Always specify "No text" unless the image is a diagram with labels
- Specify "No stock photo clichés" or "No handshake images" when relevant
